scope: Independent read-only source/test/workflow review. No test rerun, native execution, upload, POST, publish or dispatch.
findings: Workflow retains original packages only when the complete build step actually succeeded, even if installation/bootstrap/runtime subsequently fail. Both original upload steps retain exact names/order.
Export keeps exact original run/attempt/source/repo/job/build/upload/artifact identity and digest metadata, with existing bounded two-second upload-end timestamp tolerance and strict job window.
Source closure is selected from the exact checked-out source commit and each complete input is checked against its regular fixed Git blob plus recorded size/SHA256.

An ordinary failed/running/missing QA report produces built-unverified, not verifiedGames. Contradictory game/source/binary identity rejects the export. Successful reports retain both ten-test and persisted-storage checks and require successful original verify job.

Original bytes remain in download directory; a separate Git staging tree omits only validated package binaries at or above 100000000 bytes. References include exact package and original artifact identities/expiry and explicitly deny public delivery. Unrelated artifacts, symlinks, unexpected evidence or package file sets, and oversized non-package evidence reject.
No changes to success-only original-package windows-reexport verifier.
validationScope: Owner recorded 30 exporter tests + 17 prior reexport tests + actionlint passed; reviewer did not rerun them. Exact source inventory was independently rehashed. Actual prior API-derived job names and ordered build/evidence/package upload steps were inspected; full end-to-end use of the new retention branch remains future CI.
limitations: Old failed games from run 44615299245 had skipped package uploads; this change cannot recreate original missing package bytes.

Original outer artifact digest is authenticated GitHub metadata and download-artifact behavior; this exporter does not independently hash the original outer Actions ZIP. Actual package files are independently hashed against frozen manifest.
A large-file artifact reference is expiring retention, not permanent package publication or native QA success.
This review is static; no claim that future failed-build/upload paths have run on actual Windows.
